title: Quasi-affine space morphisms have affine envelopes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine scheme source after every affine scheme test. An open immersion is a representable morphism that is an open immersion on every scheme test [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be quasi-affine, meaning representable by schemes with every pullback along an affine scheme test a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Then there exist an algebraic space $Z$, a quasi-compact open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$, and an affine morphism $p:Z\to Y$ with $p\circ j=f$.

source.place: Tag 086S (lemma-characterize-quasi-affine), affine factorization consequence used in Tag 0871

proof.text: Choose a jointly surjective affine etale family $u_a:U_a\to Y$ using [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], and put $X_a=X\times_YU_a$. By the hypothesis, $X_a$ is a quasi-affine scheme. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], it is quasi-compact and absolutely separated. The affine scheme $U_a$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $f_a:X_a\to U_a$ quasi-compact. It is separated: its diagonal is the pullback of the absolute closed diagonal of $X_a$ along $X_a\times_{U_a}X_a\to X_a\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X_a$, hence is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The equivalence in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] now gives that $f$ is quasi-compact and separated.

source.place: Tag 086S (lemma-characterize-quasi-affine), reduction to affine etale charts; Tags 03KG and 03KM; scheme quasi-affineness Tag 01P9

proof.text: The structure module $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent: in the presentation definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], use the identity presentation with one generator and no relations. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-quasi-coherent-pushforward] to the quasi-compact separated $f$ from step 1. Thus $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent. Its multiplication and unit are those of sections of $\mathcal O_X$, compatible with restriction, so it is a commutative $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra. By [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence], set $Z=\operatorname{Spec}_Y\mathcal A$ with affine structural morphism $p:Z\to Y$.

source.place: Tag 081X (remark-factorization-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), first two sentences; Tags 03M9 and 081V

proof.text: Construct the map, rather than merely choosing chartwise embeddings. For the pullback/direct-image adjunction [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], the identity of $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_X$ corresponds to the evaluation counit $\epsilon:f^*\mathcal A\to\mathcal O_X$. On local tensors it sends $b\otimes a$ to $b$ times the section obtained by evaluating $a$ on the source chart; this respects products and the unit. The pullback algebra is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] over $X$ to $\epsilon$: contravariance gives a map $X=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X\to\operatorname{Spec}_X(f^*\mathcal A)=X\times_YZ$ over $X$, where the last identification is the stated base-change compatibility. Compose with the projection to $Z$ to obtain $j:X\to Z$. Its other projection is $\mathrm{id}_X$, so $p\circ j=f$.

source.place: Tag 081X (remark-factorization-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), construction from the algebra evaluation map; Tag 081V

proof.text: For each $U_a$, [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] identifies $\mathcal A|_{U_a}$ with $(f_a)_*\mathcal O_{X_a}$ by the identity on compatible sections. These identifications preserve multiplication and the unit because both are computed on the same sections. Write $C_a=\Gamma(X_a,\mathcal O_{X_a})$. The affine-chart and base-change assertions of [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] identify $Z_a=Z\times_YU_a$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_a$. Under these identifications, the map $j_a:X_a\to Z_a$ constructed in step 3 sends a global function $a\in C_a$ to that same function on $X_a$: its algebra map is exactly evaluation of $1\otimes a$. Therefore its map on global sections is $\mathrm{id}_{C_a}$. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] identifies $j_a$ with the canonical morphism $X_a\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X_a,\mathcal O_{X_a})$.

By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding] and step 4, every $j_a$ is an open immersion and its source $X_a$ is quasi-compact and absolutely separated. Its target $Z_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$ is affine, hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) to conclude that $j_a$ is quasi-compact. Also $j_a$ is separated: as in step 1 its relative diagonal is the pullback of the absolute closed diagonal of $X_a$, so use [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change].

source.place: Tag 01P9 (lemma-quasi-affine), forward implication; scheme quasi-compact permanence Tag 03GI

proof.text: The family $Z_a=Z\times_YU_a\to Z$ is jointly surjective and etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and each $Z_a$ is an affine scheme. The pullback of $j$ to $Z_a$ is $j_a$, since $X\times_Z(Z\times_YU_a)=X\times_YU_a$. By [lem-trf-space-open-immersion-etale-local], the open-immersion assertion of step 5 descends to $j$. By [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local], the quasi-compact and separated assertions of step 5 descend as well. In particular $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion. Together with the affine $p$ of step 2 and $p\circ j=f$ from step 3, this supplies the required factorization.
